source_title: Finalized authoritative structured areas are mutable, unsigned and outside correction lineage
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Migration 0128 defines `session_block_areas` as the authoritative ordered area/laterality rows and explicitly grants authenticated studio members SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE under an `FOR ALL` membership policy. The finalization trigger list predates this table and does not guard it. The signed snapshot does not include it, and the correction dispatcher has no structured-area target.
source_failure_scenario: After finalization, a practitioner—or any authenticated member able to call PostgREST—deletes “left cheek” and inserts “right cheek,” or removes all areas. The finalized status and original signed hash remain unchanged. No correction version preserves or restores the prior authoritative rows.
source_affected_users_data: Finalized treatment records, treated-area history, laterality, practitioner trust, exports and any future decision support derived from those rows.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated membership in the same studio and knowledge of a block identifier; no owner role or special service credential is required.
source_test_limitations: Migration-shape/source tests can prove the policy text but do not prove immutability. Existing finalization tests cannot cover a table that was added later unless explicitly updated.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fresh-DB test: finalize a record, then assert direct insert/update/delete and area-replacement RPC all fail; assert a reasoned correction creates immutable before/after versions; assert snapshot hash changes when area/laterality/order changes.
source_recommended_fix: Emergency containment migration: attach a finalized-parent guard to `session_block_areas`; revoke direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from `authenticated`; permit mutations only through a validated draft-only command. Add structured areas to canonical snapshot v2 and correction/amendment support. Run a production-safe audit query for post-finalization area mutations before enabling or expanding use.
source_rollout_considerations: Forward-only migration. First contain writes, then introduce snapshot v2/correction support. Do not rewrite historical signed snapshots silently; version the snapshot schema and record any remediation as an attributed correction.
source_affected_scope: multiple records within one studio; potentially multiple studios
source_current_exposure: Active in the code/schema. Whether migration 0128 is hosted-applied is reported but not independently verified; production row exposure is therefore unknown.

source_title: Finalization can race a child write and sign a state different from the committed finalized rows
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Child-table write guards perform a plain parent-status SELECT. The finalizer locks only the session row, builds the snapshot, hashes it and inserts finalization artifacts. It does not lock every child row/table or force child mutations through a lock-compatible command.
source_failure_scenario: Transaction A begins an update while the session is draft and its trigger observes draft status. Transaction B locks the session, snapshots children and finalizes. Transaction A then commits the already-authorized child mutation after the snapshot. The row is finalized, but the signed artifact describes the pre-mutation state.
source_affected_users_data: All clinical child fields guarded by the trigger model, including blocks, modality entries and images; integrity attestations and corrections.
source_prerequisites: Two overlapping authenticated requests against the same draft session.
source_test_limitations: Existing tests cover concurrent finalizer-versus-finalizer calls, not finalizer-versus-child-write interleavings. Source tests cannot establish transaction ordering.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB integration test with two independent transactions and barriers: child mutation pauses after authorization, finalizer completes, child commit must block then fail; repeat for each child table and structured areas.
source_recommended_fix: Use a single per-session advisory/row-lock protocol for every clinical mutation and finalization. Commands that mutate children should lock the parent `FOR UPDATE` before checking draft status; finalization should acquire the same lock before collecting the snapshot.
source_rollout_considerations: Ship after the P0 guard or in the same containment series. Keep finalization disabled until the concurrency test passes from a fresh DB.
source_current_exposure: Active in code; practical frequency unknown. Production exposure depends on finalization flag and real usage.

source_title: The signed finalization snapshot omits authoritative clinical fields added after the original design
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The snapshot builder serializes a subset of session/block/entry/image fields. It does not include the authoritative `session_block_areas` rows and does not cover later probe-inventory linkage and conditional numbing fields introduced by migrations 0155/0156. A successful hash therefore is not a complete representation of the record visible to a practitioner.
source_failure_scenario: Two records with different structured areas, inventory-backed probe selection or numbing details can produce snapshots that do not reflect those differences. A verifier may report the hash as valid while important chart content has changed or was never represented.
source_affected_users_data: Finalized clinical records, legal/clinical exports, dispute resolution and future audit verification.
source_prerequisites: A finalized session containing any omitted field.
source_test_limitations: Tests that assert the existence of a hash or a selected JSON shape can pass while the shape is incomplete. A completeness contract against the current schema is missing.
source_acceptance_criteria: Golden DB tests create records differing one clinically meaningful field at a time and assert canonical snapshot/hash differences; verify round-trip rendering and export from the snapshot.
source_recommended_fix: Introduce a versioned canonical snapshot schema that includes every clinically authoritative table/field, sorted deterministically. Define explicit inclusion/exclusion rules and fail finalization if an unknown required schema version is encountered.
source_rollout_considerations: Do not mutate old snapshots. Store `snapshot_schema_version`; preserve legacy version verification and use attributed corrections/backfill attestations where needed.
source_current_exposure: Active in code; production use of finalization is reported as gated/disabled and is not independently verified.

source_title: Intake submission can overwrite a concurrent practitioner edit to the client profile
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Submission uses a status compare-and-set for the intake, then separately reads the client, builds a patch from intake answers and updates the client by `id`. There is no version predicate, `updated_at` compare, field-level merge contract or transaction spanning submit and profile synchronization.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner corrects the client’s phone, birth date or other synchronized field while the client submits intake. The post-submit sync uses its earlier read and overwrites the newer practitioner value. Both actions appear successful.
source_affected_users_data: Client demographics/contact data and downstream appointment, consent and communication workflows.
source_prerequisites: Concurrent profile edit and intake submission affecting the same synchronized field.
source_test_limitations: The intake CAS test protects duplicate submission, not lost updates in the separate profile table. Ordinary unit mocks are unlikely to reproduce the interleaving.
source_acceptance_criteria: Two-connection DB test: update client after intake read but before sync; command must preserve the newer value or return a conflict requiring review.
source_recommended_fix: Move synchronization into a database command with explicit field authority and optimistic concurrency. Prefer storing intake answers as immutable submitted evidence and requiring a deliberate practitioner-reviewed merge for fields that can conflict.
source_rollout_considerations: Avoid silently re-running historical intake sync. Add a visible “profile differs from submitted intake” reconciliation state.
source_current_exposure: Active path where intake submission is enabled.

source_title: A draft intake can be marked reviewed without ever being submitted
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The review action updates the intake to `reviewed` using intake ID and studio scope. It does not require current status `submitted`, verify that the intake belongs to the route client, check one affected row, or capture a submitted version as the reviewed artifact.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner opens a client route with a stale/mismatched intake ID or triggers the action before submission. The record becomes reviewed even though answers are incomplete or still editable, creating a false clinical review signal.
source_affected_users_data: Intake status, practitioner decision-making, audit records and any booking/treatment gate relying on “reviewed.”
source_prerequisites: Authenticated same-studio member and an intake identifier.
source_test_limitations: Happy-path UI tests may only exercise submitted intake. RLS membership prevents cross-studio access but not wrong-client or wrong-state transitions within a studio.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests for draft→reviewed rejection, wrong-client rejection, duplicate review idempotency and concurrent submit/review ordering.
source_recommended_fix: Implement a database transition command requiring `status = submitted`, matching `client_id`, active practitioner attribution, submitted version/hash and exactly one affected row. Make invalid transitions fail closed.
source_rollout_considerations: Existing erroneously reviewed rows require a safe audit/reconciliation report, not silent downgrade.

source_title: The owner export is described as complete but omits material clinical, privacy, payment and media records
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The export reads a selected set of CSV datasets and explicitly excludes image binaries/storage paths and payment tables. It also omits intake/health forms, consent signatures/templates, clinical snapshots/corrections/amendments, portal messages and several audit/provenance tables. The UI says data is exportable and the README/action copy describes broad completeness.
source_failure_scenario: A studio leaves Hone, responds to an access request or needs a clinical/legal archive. The ZIP appears successful but lacks records required to reconstruct the full client history or verify finalized/corrected records. The studio may delete its account believing it has everything.
source_affected_users_data: Every studio/client, clinical/legal records, privacy requests and switching trust.
source_prerequisites: Owner runs the export and relies on its completeness.
source_test_limitations: Tests can assert expected filenames without comparing export coverage to the current schema/storage inventory.
source_acceptance_criteria: Seed one row/object in every exportable table/bucket; export, validate manifest/checksums and import into a verification tool. Test large studios and revoked/deleted records under retention policy.
source_recommended_fix: Define a versioned export manifest covering every tenant-owned table, consent/intake versions, snapshots/corrections, payment metadata, communication/audit records and image binaries with checksums. Generate a completeness report and allow independent validation.
source_rollout_considerations: Correct the UI immediately to say “partial export” until complete. Do not perform destructive offboarding based on the current artifact.
source_current_exposure: Active functionality; no complete offboarding workflow was found.

source_title: Quick Import is non-transactional and can strand clients without their treatment history
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The action bulk-inserts clients, then inserts treatment-memory rows. If memory insertion fails, the clients remain while the batch is marked voided. A retry skips existing clients, so the original file may not repair the missing history. The final completed-state update result is also not checked.
source_failure_scenario: A large import succeeds for clients but fails on one malformed/history row or transient DB error. Operators see a failed batch, retry, and receive duplicate-skips while the client profiles remain permanently detached from expected treatment memories.
source_affected_users_data: Imported clients, historical treatment context, launch data quality and support workload.
source_prerequisites: Any failure after client insert and before all memory rows/final batch transition complete.
source_test_limitations: Happy-path import tests and per-row validation do not prove atomicity or idempotent recovery after a mid-batch fault.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection DB tests at every phase; retry same batch must converge to one correct result; cross-tenant IDs and spreadsheet formula payloads must fail safely.
source_recommended_fix: Implement a transactional import RPC or staged tables with validate→preview→commit. Give every source row stable identity, upsert idempotently, persist rejected rows and support safe resume/rollback.
source_rollout_considerations: Until fixed, require verified backups and post-import reconciliation; label workflow operator-assisted and do not use it as a self-serve launch dependency.

source_title: Any authenticated practitioner can choose an arbitrary session charge amount up to CAD 2,000
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The action comments state the session price is a suggestion, accepts `amount_dollars` from the practitioner form, and permits any authenticated practitioner in the studio to initiate the charge. Stripe account, customer and payment method are server-derived, but amount authority is not owner-only or tied to an immutable invoice/service/session calculation.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner mistypes 500 instead of 50, manipulates the request, or intentionally charges an amount unrelated to the session. Idempotency can prevent duplicates but cannot make an unauthorized amount correct.
source_affected_users_data: Clients, studio funds, refunds/disputes and card-authorization evidence.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated practitioner, eligible saved card/session and live payments enabled.
source_test_limitations: Payment tests can verify amount reaches Stripe exactly as requested and still miss authorization policy. Owner-run claims are contradicted by the action.
source_acceptance_criteria: Action/DB/E2E tests reject member-supplied arbitrary values, altered hidden fields, wrong session/client/account and excessive deviations; verify receipts use the final authorized amount.
source_recommended_fix: Derive the default amount from server-authoritative services/session charges. Permit adjustments only to owners or an explicit role, with bounded reason codes, confirmation and audit. Consider dual confirmation above a threshold.
source_rollout_considerations: Before enabling another studio, reconcile existing charge attempts against expected service/session amounts and document the approved pricing authority.
source_current_exposure: Active code. Reported live production exercise is not independently verifiable.

source_title: Sentry can receive bearer credentials embedded in URL path segments
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Request and breadcrumb scrubbing removes query strings but preserves path segments. Hone places high-entropy bearer credentials in the path. The generic regexes target emails, JWTs, Bearer headers and selected token-like formats; an opaque random path segment can survive. Error events or sampled traces can therefore transmit it to Sentry.
source_failure_scenario: An exception, failed fetch breadcrumb or sampled trace occurs on a token route. The event contains the raw path. Anyone with Sentry access—or a disclosure at that processor—may replay an unexpired intake, appointment-management, portal or calendar-feed credential.
source_affected_users_data: Client health/intake data, appointment controls, portal access and private calendar feeds.
source_prerequisites: Sentry enabled and an event/trace on a bearer-path route before token expiry/revocation.
source_test_limitations: Unit tests that scrub query parameters/JWTs may pass without opaque path-token cases. PostHog has a stronger route boundary, but Sentry does not inherit it.
source_acceptance_criteria: Sentry scrub tests with realistic opaque tokens in request URL, transaction, span description, breadcrumb and exception context; assert the token never appears in serialized event JSON.
source_recommended_fix: Canonicalize sensitive routes to templates before Sentry processing, e.g. `/intake/[token]`; drop transaction names/URLs/breadcrumb data for all bearer routes; add server-side allowlisted route metadata instead. Rotate/revoke credentials after suspected leakage.
source_rollout_considerations: Deploy scrub before enabling tracing broadly. Review Sentry retention/access and search historical events for route patterns without exporting raw tokens.
source_exact_source_location: `lib/observability/sentry-scrub.ts:183-190,213-222,320-324`; token routes under `app/intake/[token]`, cancel/manage/reschedule, portal verification and `app/calendar-feed/[token]`
source_current_exposure: Gated by Sentry configuration, but active code posture.

source_title: Availability, overrides, blockouts and service scheduling settings remain directly writable by any studio member
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Early RLS grants full membership-scoped DML to schedule configuration tables. Later atomic/locked owner actions improve the intended path but do not remove the direct table capability.
source_failure_scenario: A non-owner practitioner or compromised member account edits another practitioner’s availability, removes blockouts, changes service settings or races a booking without the owner checks, locking and audit semantics in the newer actions.
source_affected_users_data: All practitioners and clients in a studio; booking reliability and operational trust.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated studio membership.
source_test_limitations: UI tests can confirm owner-only controls while direct PostgREST remains available. Negative grant/RLS tests are needed.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests assert members cannot modify another practitioner/studio-wide settings; approved commands serialize with public/internal booking.
source_recommended_fix: Revoke broad DML; separate owner-managed studio policy, practitioner self-availability and system materialization commands. Each command should lock the same capacity authority used by booking.
source_rollout_considerations: Coordinate with public-booking command migration so there is one consistent lock protocol.
source_exact_source_location: `supabase/migrations/0010_booking_v1.sql:237-270`; compare owner-locked writers in migrations `0149` and `0150`

source_title: Public booking ignores the practitioner-capacity emergency booking kill switch
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Internal booking V2 locks the studio/capacity state and checks the booking-enabled control. Public booking inserts directly through the admin client after a slot recheck and never calls the authoritative command or the kill-switch check.
source_failure_scenario: An operator disables booking during a capacity incident or migration. Internal creation stops, but anonymous clients continue creating public appointments, defeating the emergency containment mechanism.
source_affected_users_data: Studio calendar, clients, practitioners and incident response.
source_prerequisites: A studio with public booking enabled while the capacity/system gate is disabled.
source_test_limitations: Tests limited to the internal command can pass. A cross-entry-point gate test is missing.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB/browser test toggles the kill switch between slot display and submit; submission must fail with a safe unavailable message and create no client/appointment side effects.
source_recommended_fix: Route all public appointment creation through a public-safe authoritative DB command that checks global/studio/practitioner gates under the capacity lock immediately before insert.
source_rollout_considerations: Ship before relying on the kill switch operationally or enabling multi-practitioner public booking.
source_current_exposure: Active code path; current flag use in production unknown.

source_title: Public booking is outside the capacity lock and can race schedule edits or authoritative internal commands
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Public booking performs a slot recheck in application code and later inserts directly. It does not acquire the same studio/practitioner capacity lock used by internal booking and schedule writers, so the check and insert are not serialized with an availability change.
source_failure_scenario: A public slot is rechecked as available. At the same time, an owner saves an override/blockout or another command reserves capacity. The public insert commits based on stale policy. A unique overlap constraint may catch exact appointment overlap, but not all buffer, capacity, archive or policy races.
source_affected_users_data: Public clients, practitioner schedules, buffers and launch incident containment.
source_prerequisites: Concurrent public submit and schedule/capacity mutation.
source_test_limitations: Sequential tests and source assertions do not prove interleaving. Existing overlap tests may cover only hard appointment collision.
source_acceptance_criteria: Two-connection tests for public booking versus override, blockout, service archive, practitioner deactivation, internal booking and kill-switch toggle.
source_recommended_fix: Move public booking into the same DB transaction/lock protocol as internal creation; derive service duration and practitioner eligibility under lock; atomically create client/consent/appointment/audit or return no side effects.
source_rollout_considerations: Requires a compatibility wrapper for the anonymous/token surface; do not expose a broadly executable unsafe RPC.

source_title: DST conversion silently shifts nonexistent local times and cannot represent the second repeated hour
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The helper explicitly documents that a Toronto spring-forward local time such as 02:30 maps one hour before the requested wall time, and a fall-back repeated 01:xx resolves to the first occurrence. Booking/move actions do not round-trip validate the selected wall time or expose an occurrence choice.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner enters 02:30 on spring-forward day and Hone records 01:30. On fall-back day, the second 01:30 cannot be selected. Reminders, calendar rendering, Google events and client expectations can disagree by an hour.
source_affected_users_data: Appointments near DST transitions in any supported timezone with gaps/overlaps.
source_prerequisites: Use of a nonexistent or ambiguous local time.
source_test_limitations: Existing tests may encode the current mapping as expected behaviour, creating false confidence rather than rejecting ambiguity.
source_acceptance_criteria: Unit and browser tests for Toronto/New York spring-forward and fall-back, midnight boundaries, long services and Google/notification rendering.
source_recommended_fix: Use a timezone library/API that detects nonexistent and ambiguous wall times. Reject gaps with a clear UI message. For overlaps, require/derive an explicit offset/occurrence and round-trip validate before writing.
source_rollout_considerations: Data audit for appointments created in transition windows; do not automatically shift historical rows without practitioner review.

source_title: A same-studio member can re-parent a draft clinical session to the wrong client through direct DML
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Session and block policies are membership-scoped. The identity-freeze trigger protects selected session identity fields only after finalization. While draft, an authenticated studio member can update `client_id` directly if the row remains in the same studio.
source_failure_scenario: A buggy client, malicious practitioner or copied UUID changes a draft session from Client A to Client B. Existing blocks/entries now appear under the wrong client, potentially exposing sensitive history and causing future treatment decisions to use another person’s record.
source_affected_users_data: Client clinical histories, practitioner attribution, photos and treatment-memory views.
source_prerequisites: Same-studio membership and access to a draft session ID and another client ID.
source_test_limitations: Cross-tenant tests can pass because studio IDs remain correct. A same-tenant wrong-client negative test is required.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests reject direct client/studio/practitioner re-parenting in draft and finalized states; test approved command only under owner/authorized role with audit event.
source_recommended_fix: Freeze session identity from creation except through a dedicated audited reassignment command with strict no-child or explicit migration semantics. Revoke direct UPDATE on identity columns from authenticated users.
source_rollout_considerations: Audit existing sessions for identity changes where history permits. Avoid a blanket rewrite of affected records.
source_affected_scope: one client or multiple clients in a studio
source_current_exposure: Active in code; direct PostgREST access is available under table grants/policies.

source_title: Broad authenticated appointment DML bypasses owner/member command authorization, invariants and audit
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The appointment table is exposed under broad studio-membership DML while newer create/move commands implement role checks, capacity locks, authoritative duration and availability validation. A caller can bypass the newer command by calling PostgREST directly.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner changes duration, assignment, status or times directly, bypassing owner-only override rules, buffer semantics, kill switches and expected audit side effects. The database row may be valid structurally while violating scheduling policy.
source_affected_users_data: Appointments, practitioner calendars, client notifications, payment eligibility and audit history.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated studio membership and direct Supabase API access.
source_test_limitations: Server-action tests prove the command path, not that alternate table writes are impossible.
source_acceptance_criteria: Direct DML negative tests for every restricted field/status transition; command tests assert locks, authority, audit and one-row effects.
source_recommended_fix: Revoke authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on appointments; expose narrow SECURITY DEFINER commands for create, move, cancel, complete, no-show and approved administrative repair. Use column privileges as an intermediate containment step.
source_rollout_considerations: Stage behind feature flags only if legacy clients require migration; instrument denied direct writes and provide an operator repair command.
source_current_exposure: Active in schema. Whether browser code currently invokes it is irrelevant to direct-call risk.

source_title: SaaS subscription billing and entitlements are absent
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Stripe Connect client payments are distinct from billing studios for Hone. There is no demonstrated plan subscription, dunning, entitlement, trial, cancellation, invoice/tax or access-suspension control plane.
source_failure_scenario: Paid acquisition requires manual invoicing and feature flags; failed payment does not map safely to access or data-retention state.
source_affected_users_data: Hone revenue operations and every paying studio.
source_prerequisites: Commercial rollout beyond founder-managed pilots.
source_test_limitations: Payment tests for client charges do not cover SaaS billing.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fake-provider subscription lifecycle tests including duplicate/out-of-order webhooks, dunning, plan changes and cancellation.
source_recommended_fix: After the safety pilot, build separate platform-billing customer/subscription/entitlement models with webhook idempotency, grace periods, manual override audit and no coupling to clinical data deletion.
source_rollout_considerations: Defer until studio #2 safety; required before scaling paid acquisition.
source_exact_source_location: No complete subscription/customer/plan/entitlement lifecycle found in archive

source_title: Calendar-feed bearer URLs lack rotation/revocation UI and last-used telemetry
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The feed uses a high-entropy bearer URL, hash-only storage and generic busy content—good privacy foundations. The route comments defer a user-facing rotate/revoke capability, and no clear last-used telemetry is exposed.
source_failure_scenario: A feed URL is pasted into the wrong service, appears in logs or a device is lost. The owner cannot easily rotate it or see whether it is still used, so exposure persists until manual intervention/expiry policy.
source_prerequisites: Token leakage or device change.
source_test_limitations: Route tests may validate hash and generic content but not lifecycle UX.
source_acceptance_criteria: Browser/route tests verify old token revocation, new token activation and no raw token in telemetry/Sentry.
source_recommended_fix: Add owner-controlled rotate/revoke, overlapping cutover window, last-used timestamp/client fingerprint minimization and alerts for unusual use.
source_rollout_considerations: Coordinate with F-PRIV-001 before broader feed use.
source_current_exposure: Active if feed feature is enabled.

source_title: Hosting, encryption and compliance-facing UI claims are not fully supported by evidence in the ZIP

source_evidence: The action loops day by day up to its horizon and invokes slot generation repeatedly. Each day can issue several DB reads. Sparse calendars and public abuse can multiply latency and load.
source_failure_scenario: A studio has no availability for weeks. One anonymous request performs many sequential queries; concurrent users amplify load and tie up serverless execution.
source_prerequisites: Sparse availability or abuse.
source_test_limitations: Unit tests on a few dates do not measure query count/latency.
source_acceptance_criteria: Benchmark sparse/dense calendars at 10/50/100 studios and assert maximum query/time budget.
source_recommended_fix: Query/materialize candidate availability in bounded ranges, cache safe schedule inputs, paginate search and enforce a request work budget with metrics.
source_rollout_considerations: Address before paid traffic; do not optimize ahead of correctness/atomicity.

source_title: Public multi-practitioner booking is not implemented safely; appointments resolve to owner or null
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The public action looks up the studio owner and assigns that practitioner (or null). It does not expose a validated practitioner choice, no-preference allocation or capacity-aware assignment.
source_failure_scenario: A multi-practitioner studio publishes booking expecting team availability. Public appointments land on the owner or unassigned, distorting capacity and requiring manual repair.
source_affected_users_data: Studios with more than one practitioner and their clients.
source_prerequisites: Multi-practitioner public launch.
source_test_limitations: Schema/capacity tests do not establish public allocation behaviour.
source_acceptance_criteria: Browser/DB tests for chosen practitioner, no preference, parallel practitioners, deactivation, reassignment and cross-studio practitioner substitution.
source_recommended_fix: Add explicit service-practitioner eligibility, practitioner choice/no-preference policy and atomic assignment under the capacity lock. Do not infer readiness from schema alone.
source_rollout_considerations: Keep public multi-practitioner disabled until a controlled pilot passes.
source_current_exposure: Implemented code is solo-owner oriented; broad pilot exposure unknown.

source_title: Slot generation ignores several database query errors and can return misleading availability
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Blockout, capacity/default and reservation queries consume `.data` without consistently surfacing `.error`. A failed query can be interpreted as no blockouts/reservations or missing defaults rather than an unavailable scheduling service.
source_failure_scenario: A transient DB/RLS/query error omits a conflict input. Hone shows a slot that should be blocked, or returns an empty/misleading calendar with no operational alert.
source_prerequisites: Any relevant query error.
source_test_limitations: Mocks that return data only do not exercise error branches.
source_acceptance_criteria: Unit tests inject each query error; public submit must revalidate and create no booking; UI distinguishes “no availability” from system failure.
source_recommended_fix: Fail closed for mutation-relevant availability, return a distinct temporary-unavailable state, emit redacted ops metrics and avoid caching incomplete results.
source_rollout_considerations: Ship with public atomic command; do not expose provider/database details.
source_affected_scope: one studio to production-wide during outage

source_title: Treatment-image upload can leave orphaned private objects when metadata insertion and cleanup both fail
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: The action uploads the object first, then inserts metadata. On metadata failure it attempts deletion and emits an alert if cleanup fails. There is no durable reconciliation queue or periodic orphan scanner shown.
source_failure_scenario: Storage upload succeeds, DB insert fails, and cleanup fails transiently. The object remains private but untracked, cannot be exported through metadata and may persist indefinitely.
source_affected_users_data: Client images, retention obligations and storage cost.
source_prerequisites: Cross-system partial failure.
source_test_limitations: Mocked cleanup tests cannot prove eventual reconciliation.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection tests for every failure point and reconciler convergence without cross-tenant deletion.
source_recommended_fix: Create a durable upload intent/object ledger and reconciler; use deterministic state transitions, checksums and retention-safe quarantine. Periodically compare bucket objects to metadata.
source_rollout_considerations: Do not expose orphan paths; preserve incident/audit evidence.

source_title: A large source-string assertion surface creates false confidence about runtime behaviour
source_baseline_sha: (the July-27 audit states no repository SHA; its §1.2 source identity is ZIP comment 058b8bcbd1a80d6aa89c47f9357e1964328f220d, SHA-256 160b2789d6e093ca0ef6cd20560ae2ed49fe9c831242622a03c371f13dd2c324)
source_evidence: Source/migration shape tests are useful guardrails, but many assert that strings, comments, function names or fragments exist. They cannot prove RLS under real roles, transaction isolation, provider request semantics or UI behaviour.
source_failure_scenario: A refactor can preserve asserted text while behaviour is unsafe, or safe behaviour can break tests because formatting changes. Passing counts may be presented as stronger evidence than they are.
source_affected_users_data: All critical workflows and release decisions.
source_prerequisites: Reliance on aggregate test count without coverage classification.
source_test_limitations: This finding is about evidence quality, not a claim that all source tests are bad. The local DB harness is a strong counterexample.
source_acceptance_criteria: Coverage map must identify the behavioural layer for every P0/P1 regression and fail releases that have source-only coverage.
source_recommended_fix: Label test classes in CI; shift highest-risk assertions to DB/browser/concurrency/provider-contract behaviour; retain source guards only for truly static invariants.
source_rollout_considerations: Incremental conversion; do not delete guards until stronger tests exist.
source_exact_source_location: Static inventory: 339 test files use `readFileSync` (824 occurrences); 171 use `toContain` (742 occurrences); migration/source guards throughout `tests/`
source_current_exposure: Active test design; execution unavailable here.
unscheduled_reason: P3 assurance gap; no PR in this tranche.

source_evidence: The suite covers selected duplicate/finalizer cases and hard-overlap scenarios, but the two confirmed races do not have two-connection barrier tests that reproduce their transaction ordering.
source_failure_scenario: A future change passes all ordinary tests while preserving or reintroducing a signed-snapshot mismatch or stale public-booking commit.
source_prerequisites: Concurrent requests.
source_test_limitations: Sequential browser/unit tests cannot establish serialization.
source_acceptance_criteria: The regression itself is the required evidence: old code must fail, fixed code must pass reliably across repeated runs.
source_recommended_fix: Add deterministic two-connection DB tests with synchronization barriers and repeat under relevant isolation levels. Test every entry point against the same lock authority.
source_rollout_considerations: Run in mandatory DB CI, not an optional slow lane.

source_title: Authenticated members can bypass audited soft deletion of treatment passes
source_evidence: `supabase/migrations/0087_clinical_rls_delete_hardening.sql:217–263` retains authenticated DELETE policies; `0114_entry_soft_delete.sql:3–25` adds an audited soft-delete triad but does not revoke DELETE.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated active studio membership and an entry identifier
source_acceptance_criteria: No interactive tenant role can physically delete a treatment-pass row.
source_recommended_fix: Drop both member DELETE policies; revoke DELETE on both tables from `authenticated`/`anon`; reserve physical purge for a controlled retention job.
source_risk_at_stake: Permanent loss of clinical treatment-pass history and deletion without actor/reason metadata
source_business_impact: A practitioner or compromised account can erase history that the product presents as treatment memory and bypass the 0114 audit fields.
source_existing_controls: RLS requires the related session to be visible; the intended application action performs an UPDATE with `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, and reason.
source_why_controls_insufficient: UI behavior is not authorization. The database still authorizes physical deletion.
source_required_regression_tests: Direct same-studio DELETE denied; cross-studio DELETE denied; authorized soft-delete succeeds; purge role only works after retention/legal-hold checks.
source_reproduction: In local Supabase, authenticate as a member, identify a visible electrolysis or laser entry, and issue a direct table DELETE instead of the UI action.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Any use of Hone as a treatment record; controlled studio; unrelated studios

source_title: Treatment-image storage hardening can silently remain unapplied
source_evidence: `0092_treatment_images.sql` creates authenticated storage-object policies; `0093_harden_treatment_image_storage.sql` catches `insufficient_privilege`, raises a notice, and lets the migration continue.
source_prerequisites: Hosted migration role lacks permission to modify storage bucket metadata or object policies
source_acceptance_criteria: Photo enablement is blocked when hosted storage posture differs from the approved manifest.
source_recommended_fix: Add a read-only storage-posture verifier; fail photo enablement and release attestation unless bucket privacy and the exact approved policies match.
source_risk_at_stake: Sensitive image objects may retain broader access than the application and migration comments assume
source_business_impact: A release can report a successful database migration while a separate hosted storage boundary remains in the old state.
source_confidence: High for repository risk; hosted state unknown
source_existing_controls: Server-generated paths, private-bucket intent, image sanitization, parent checks, 60-second signed URLs, and metadata rows scoped by studio/client.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Those application controls do not prove hosted bucket privacy or the absence of stale object policies.
source_required_regression_tests: Local storage policy tests; hosted read-only verifier; cross-studio object-list/read/write denial; signed-URL ownership/expiry tests.
source_reproduction: Apply the migrations under a role that cannot alter the platform-owned storage objects, then inspect bucket privacy and policies.
source_confidence_rating: High for repository risk; hosted state unknown
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Any storage of real treatment photos; unrelated studios

source_title: No attested production source of truth
source_evidence: The ZIP has no `.git`; CI explicitly does not deploy; no Vercel/Supabase/Stripe/provider export or release manifest was supplied.
source_prerequisites: Any drift between ZIP, deployed artifact, database, storage, cron, or provider configuration
source_acceptance_criteria: Every production state can be traced to an immutable source revision and approved hosted-control manifest.
source_recommended_fix: Generate and retain a non-secret release attestation covering build SHA, migration max, critical DDL/policy hashes, storage posture, job schedules, Stripe mode, and feature flags.
source_risk_at_stake: Review conclusions may not describe the system handling real data or money
source_business_impact: A correct repository can coexist with stale code, unapplied migrations, permissive policies, wrong provider mode, or disabled jobs.
source_existing_controls: CI covers typecheck, lint/build, unit, local database, Stripe-gate, and E2E lanes by design.
source_why_controls_insufficient: CI success is not deployment, hosted configuration, feature enablement, or production exercise.
source_required_regression_tests: Attestation generated in staging and production; mismatch blocks promotion; rollback produces its own attestation.
source_reproduction: Compare a future read-only production build SHA, migration history, policy hashes, storage posture, cron registry, and provider modes with this archive.

source_title: Cross-studio platform administration is authorized by email allowlist
source_evidence: `lib/admin.ts:1–72` resolves `ADMIN_EMAILS`; comments state membership grants cross-studio access through the service-role client; `0113_admin_action_events.sql` adds an admin audit table but not a durable role model.
source_prerequisites: Compromise or reassignment of an allowlisted Supabase identity/email
source_acceptance_criteria: An allowlisted email alone never unlocks service-role operations.
source_recommended_fix: Create platform roles, require Supabase AAL2/MFA for elevation, use short privileged sessions, least-privilege actions, and complete audit coverage.
source_risk_at_stake: Service-role reads/writes across every studio
source_business_impact: The highest privilege boundary has no database-backed role lifecycle, AAL2 requirement, expiry, approval, or scoped support capability.
source_existing_controls: Production fails closed when `ADMIN_EMAILS` is absent; admin actions increasingly create append-only events.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Email possession plus an ordinary authenticated session remains the privilege grant.
source_required_regression_tests: AAL1 denial; AAL2 success; role revocation; stale session denial; scoped support role; every mutation emits an immutable event.
source_reproduction: In local/staging, authenticate an identity whose email is in `ADMIN_EMAILS` and access `/admin`; compare with a non-allowlisted user.
source_affected_personas: Platform administrators; all tenants affected by compromise
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Second unrelated studio; ten studios; public SaaS

source_title: Public self-service SaaS lifecycle is absent
source_evidence: No runtime `supabase.auth.signUp`, public studio-creation route, Stripe Checkout/subscription flow, plan/entitlement model, dunning, billing portal, or automated cancellation lifecycle was found; studio creation is under `/admin/studios/new`.
source_prerequisites: A studio owner has not been manually provisioned by Hone
source_acceptance_criteria: A stranger can become an active paying studio and leave without database, provider-dashboard, environment, or code intervention.
source_recommended_fix: Implement signup/provisioning, subscription billing, entitlements, activation, support, and offboarding as separate gated systems.
source_risk_at_stake: Activation, revenue, access, support, and offboarding depend on founder/admin intervention
source_business_impact: Hone is a founder-operated product, not self-service SaaS.
source_existing_controls: A setup checklist and founder-led onboarding exist; the public site uses founding-pilot language.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Guided configuration does not replace atomic provisioning, subscription state, entitlement enforcement, or cancellation.
source_required_regression_tests: Duplicate signup, failed provisioning rollback, webhook replay/order, downgrade enforcement, dunning/grace, cancellation/reactivation, data access and purge.
source_reproduction: Start at the public site and attempt to create, fund, configure, activate, bill, cancel, and delete a studio without admin access.
source_affected_feature: Signup, tenant provisioning, Hone billing, entitlements, cancellation
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Public signup; ten studios without founder setup; scale

source_recommended_fix: Define organization/location/resource entities and explicit sharing/authorization rules before adding location UI.
source_risk_at_stake: Incorrect schedules, pricing, tax, communications, payment, permissions, and reporting
source_business_impact: The product cannot represent the scenario without misusing “studio” as both tenant and location.

source_why_controls_insufficient: Several independent studios are not one organization with shared clients, central billing, and local operational scope.
source_required_regression_tests: Cross-location membership, shared/separate clients, resource collisions, local pricing/tax, location booking pages, central reporting, audit scope.

source_affected_personas: Multi-location owner, practitioner, central/local admin, client

source_title: Required scheduled-job activation is not declaratively complete
source_evidence: Three cron handlers exist, while `vercel.json` schedules only recurring-break materialization; repository notes indicate reminders may depend on an external scheduler; production activation was not supplied.
source_prerequisites: External scheduler is absent, misconfigured, duplicated, or silently failing

source_recommended_fix: Declare all jobs in one registry; expose last/next run, claimed/sent/failed counts, retries, and alerts; disable duplicate schedulers.
source_risk_at_stake: Missed/duplicate communications, stale calendar state, hidden operational backlog
source_business_impact: A code-complete automation may never execute—or may execute twice.
source_confidence: High on repository mismatch; hosted activation unknown

source_why_controls_insufficient: There is no single authoritative job registry, health view, dead-letter queue, or owner.
source_required_regression_tests: Auth, duplicate invocation, provider outage, retry exhaustion, cancellation/suspension, time-zone and daylight-saving behavior.
source_reproduction: Inventory all hosted schedulers, compare route/schedule/secret/environment, then inspect last-success and duplicate-run evidence.
source_confidence_rating: High on repository mismatch; hosted activation unknown

source_title: Reusable calendar-feed bearer credentials are readable at studio-member scope
source_evidence: `0046_practitioner_calendar_feed_token.sql` adds raw token; `0079_calendar_feed_token_hash.sql` adds a hash but retains raw column; practitioner member SELECT policies and `lib/supabase/queries.ts` broad practitioner reads expose the row.
source_prerequisites: A member can read another practitioner row or a broad `select('*')` result
source_acceptance_criteria: No tenant query returns a reusable calendar-feed secret.
source_recommended_fix: Move feed credentials to a private service-only table, store only a hash, show raw once, add rotation/revocation and access events.
source_risk_at_stake: Long-lived feed access to client appointment information
source_business_impact: Ordinary membership can become access to another practitioner’s reusable external calendar URL.
source_existing_controls: A hash lookup path was added; feed route token is unguessable; membership can be revoked.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Keeping the raw secret on a broadly readable tenant table defeats hash-at-rest and least privilege.
source_required_regression_tests: Member cannot read credential; valid feed works; old token fails after rotation; former member/feed revocation; rate limit and no sensitive logs.
source_reproduction: In local Supabase as practitioner A, query visible practitioner B and inspect `calendar_feed_token`; use it against `/calendar-feed/[token]`.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Multi-practitioner studio; unrelated studios after credential leakage

source_title: Completed treatment history has no enforced finalization or amendment model
source_evidence: Sessions do not carry an enforced finalized/version state; `DoneChartingButton` is navigation/UI completion; member UPDATE policies remain for sessions and entries.
source_prerequisites: Authorized member edits a prior session or entry
source_acceptance_criteria: Every post-finalization change is an explicit attributable amendment that preserves prior values.
source_recommended_fix: Add draft/finalized/amended states, row versions, immutable snapshots, server-only amendment RPCs, reason/actor/timestamp, and deny direct terminal updates.
source_risk_at_stake: Silent rewriting of areas, settings, observations, notes, and “last visit” context
source_business_impact: The exact history feeding treatment memory can change without an attributable amendment.
source_existing_controls: Session/entry audit tables and soft-delete fields exist in parts of the model.
source_why_controls_insufficient: An audit insert that is optional/fail-soft does not make the underlying state immutable.
source_required_regression_tests: Draft edit allowed; finalize atomic; terminal direct update/delete denied; amendment preserves original; concurrent version conflict; audit event mandatory.
source_reproduction: Complete a session in the UI, then directly update its earlier entries/notes through the authenticated client.
source_affected_personas: Practitioners, owners, clients relying on records
source_affected_feature: Sessions, treatment entries, notes, treatment memory

source_title: Submitted or reviewed intake responses can be overwritten directly
source_evidence: Public actions restrict changes by workflow state, but member UPDATE RLS on intake response rows does not prohibit terminal-state mutation; direct authenticated data access bypasses UI guards.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated studio membership and intake row access
source_acceptance_criteria: Submitted intake content is immutable except through an attributable versioned amendment workflow.
source_recommended_fix: Freeze submitted responses; use versioned amendment/reopen operations with actor/reason and preserve the original submission snapshot/hash.
source_risk_at_stake: Contraindication answers, review state, and the historical basis for treatment can silently change
source_business_impact: The record shown as submitted/reviewed may not be the record the client originally supplied.
source_existing_controls: Intake links/tokens, save-vs-submit behavior, review fields, and application validation exist.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Application-state checks are not enforced at the database boundary.
source_required_regression_tests: In-progress update allowed; terminal direct update denied; authorized reopen creates new version; contraindication/review history retained.
source_reproduction: Submit an intake locally, authenticate as a studio member, and update a response value directly through Supabase.
source_affected_feature: Client health/intake forms and review status
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Any broad storage of real intake data

source_title: Appointment collision constraint treats the whole studio as one resource
source_evidence: `0030_calendar_reservations.sql` exclusion constraint keys active appointment time range by `studio_id`, not practitioner/room/resource.
source_prerequisites: Two valid appointments overlap in one studio
source_acceptance_criteria: Parallel legitimate appointments succeed while every exclusive resource remains race-safe.
source_recommended_fix: Introduce explicit appointment resource/practitioner scope and exclusion constraints for the resources that must not overlap.
source_risk_at_stake: Legitimate parallel capacity is rejected; workarounds can weaken collision safety
source_business_impact: The data model is effectively single-resource even though team membership exists.
source_existing_controls: Database exclusion provides strong race-safe double-booking prevention for the current model.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Correct concurrency control is applied to the wrong business resource.
source_required_regression_tests: Same practitioner collision denied; different practitioners allowed; shared room/device collision denied; reschedule/override/DST and concurrent final-slot tests.
source_reproduction: Create two practitioners in one studio and attempt non-conflicting appointments at the same time.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Any studio with simultaneous practitioners; multi-location

source_title: Core tenant audit evidence is user-insertable and not uniformly transaction-mandatory
source_evidence: Legacy audit tables have member INSERT policies; several actions perform a state mutation followed by a separate audit insert and tolerate/log audit failure.
source_prerequisites: Member inserts fabricated audit row or a state write succeeds while audit write fails
source_acceptance_criteria: Every critical state transition has one durable, non-user-forgeable event.
source_recommended_fix: Move critical audit emission into SECURITY DEFINER RPCs/triggers with safe `search_path`, derive actor/studio from auth/context, and revoke member INSERT.
source_risk_at_stake: False attribution, missing evidence, and unreliable reconstruction
source_business_impact: Audit history can be forged or absent precisely when needed for consent, clinical, payment, or security review.
source_existing_controls: `admin_action_events` is stronger: no normal-user policies and service-role writes; several newer operations write structured events.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Not all critical changes use an actor-derived, append-only, atomic server/database path.
source_required_regression_tests: Forged insert denied; mutation rolls back if mandatory audit fails; actor/studio cannot be overridden; immutable read path; retention independent from parent deletion.
source_reproduction: Insert a plausible audit event as a member, or force the audit insert to fail after the underlying update in local/staging.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Authoritative records; unrelated studios; incident response

source_title: Stripe live permission is deployment-wide rather than canonical per studio
source_evidence: `lib/stripe/server.ts:44–66,119–130` gates the Stripe secret by environment/key prefix; it does not establish a database-enforced studio approval state across every mutation.
source_prerequisites: Production uses a live key with `STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE_MODE=true`
source_acceptance_criteria: Every live mutation proves an active per-studio approval and matching Connect account/mode.
source_recommended_fix: Add a studio payment-capability state machine (`disabled`, `test`, `live_pending`, `live_approved`, `suspended`) enforced server-side in all Stripe mutations and refunds.
source_risk_at_stake: A reachable studio/payment path may gain live-money capability beyond the explicitly approved tenant
source_business_impact: The operational promise “only approved studios are live” is not enforced by one canonical tenant state.
source_existing_controls: Studio/account ownership and livemode are recorded in payment tables; UI settings can hold features.
source_why_controls_insufficient: A deployment environment flag answers “may this process use a live key,” not “may this studio perform this live operation.”
source_required_regression_tests: Unapproved live mutation denied; approved succeeds; suspension immediate; account replacement/reconnect; webhook cannot elevate capability.
source_reproduction: In test/staging, enable the equivalent live-mode flag and invoke payment setup/charge paths for an unapproved studio.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Controlled live studio; broad live rollout

source_title: “Full data export” is incomplete and memory-bound
source_evidence: `app/(app)/settings/data/actions.ts` exports selected CSVs and explicitly excludes image/payment data; archive assembly is synchronous/in-memory/base64 and omits several sensitive/ledger domains.
source_prerequisites: Studio requests all data or has significant history/photos
source_acceptance_criteria: The export manifest exactly matches product/legal copy and completes within defined size/SLO limits.
source_recommended_fix: Define a versioned export manifest; add asynchronous job/object delivery; include all required metadata/binaries or clearly document exclusions.
source_risk_at_stake: Missing health, consent, image, payment, communication, and audit evidence; process failure on large archives
source_business_impact: Marketing/terms portability claims are unsupported and offboarding cannot preserve a complete record.
source_existing_controls: An owner data-export UI exists and covers useful core entities.
source_why_controls_insufficient: A partial application export is not a complete portable studio record and will not scale with photo volume.
source_required_regression_tests: Fixture coverage for every domain; tenant isolation; soft-deleted/audit history; large export; resumability; integrity hash; expiring authenticated download.
source_reproduction: Create a studio with intake, signed consent, photos, payments/refunds, communications, portal events, audit and soft-deleted history; compare export contents.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Public SaaS, cancellation, DSAR, migration to another system

source_title: Tenant authorization is predominantly coarse studio-member access
source_evidence: Many policies use `is_studio_member(studio_id)`; owner checks exist for selected settings/actions, but no complete capability/role matrix or reception/support model was found.
source_prerequisites: A member should have narrower duties than full studio clinical/data access
source_acceptance_criteria: Every operation is denied unless the active studio role has its explicit capability.
source_recommended_fix: Create a capability model for owner/practitioner/staff, enforce it in RLS/RPC/server actions, and test every high-risk object/action.
source_risk_at_stake: Over-broad access to intake, treatment, photos, configuration, exports, or destructive actions
source_business_impact: Adding staff or unrelated practitioners creates privacy and insider-risk exposure.
source_existing_controls: Studio membership and some owner-only server actions; RLS is enabled across repository tables.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Tenant isolation from other studios does not establish least privilege within a studio.
source_required_regression_tests: Role matrix across clients/intake/consent/photos/charting/settings/payments/export/team/audit; revoked membership; cross-tab stale role.
source_reproduction: Create owner and practitioner memberships and exercise direct table/API operations beyond each persona’s intended UI.

source_title: Clinical and intake edits lack optimistic concurrency protection
source_evidence: No consistent row `version`/ETag/compare-and-swap pattern was found for mutable clinical/intake records.
source_prerequisites: Two tabs/users edit the same mutable record
source_acceptance_criteria: A stale client cannot silently overwrite a newer clinical/intake version.
source_recommended_fix: Add version columns and conditional updates, conflict UI, draft autosave timestamps, and immutable finalization.
source_risk_at_stake: Last-write-wins loss of observations, settings, warnings, or notes
source_business_impact: A practitioner can unknowingly overwrite another person’s treatment documentation.
source_existing_controls: Some operations are discrete rows; database transactions/constraints exist for selected workflows.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Those controls do not detect stale edits to the same record.
source_required_regression_tests: Two-editor conflict; stale offline save; retry after conflict; no duplicate audit/amendment.
source_reproduction: Open the same session in two clients, save conflicting changes in sequence, and inspect the lost update.
source_affected_launch_scenarios: Multi-user studios; long sessions; unstable networks

source_title: Privacy retention, deletion, correction, and offboarding are not complete operational workflows
source_evidence: Soft deletion exists in selected domains, but no complete case workflow, retention schedule, legal hold, provider purge, backup evidence, portal/job revocation, or permanent-deletion orchestration was found.
source_prerequisites: Access/correction/deletion/withdrawal request, retention expiry, legal hold, or studio cancellation
source_acceptance_criteria: Every lifecycle request has an attributable state, scope, deadline, completion evidence, and exception path.
source_recommended_fix: Define retention classes and a case-based export/correct/delete/hold workflow with evidence, approval, purge queue, and exception reporting.
source_risk_at_stake: Inconsistent deletion, residual jobs/tokens/objects/provider data, loss of required records, or unfulfilled policy promise
source_business_impact: Sensitive-data obligations and policy promises depend on ad hoc manual work.
source_existing_controls: Some client soft-delete, token status checks, export UI, and audit events exist.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Data lifecycle spans providers and immutable/required records; individual delete actions are insufficient.
source_required_regression_tests: Client/studio request matrix; hold prevents purge; provider failures retry; tokens/jobs revoked; required audit retained; backup handling documented/tested.

source_title: Losing a final-slot booking race can leave client/consent side effects
source_evidence: `app/book/[slug]/actions.ts` creates/updates client and consent state before the appointment insert; the exclusion violation returns without rolling those earlier side effects back.
source_prerequisites: Two clients submit the final slot concurrently
source_acceptance_criteria: A rejected booking creates no durable side effect beyond an abuse/rate-limit event.
source_recommended_fix: Move client upsert, consent capture, appointment creation, token/audit creation into one database transaction/RPC, or cleanly stage pending records.
source_risk_at_stake: Orphan/updated client and consent records even though appointment creation loses the exclusion race
source_business_impact: Failed booking attempts can pollute CRM/consent data and trigger confusing follow-up.
source_existing_controls: Appointment insert is race-safe and confirmations are not sent after the exclusion error.
source_why_controls_insufficient: The broader booking workflow is not one atomic transaction.
source_required_regression_tests: Concurrent final slot; duplicate submit; retry; existing/new client; no email/SMS/audit on rejected transaction.
source_reproduction: Submit the same final slot concurrently with new client identities and inspect client/consent rows for the rejected request.

source_title: Public booking silently assigns the active owner and offers no practitioner selection

source_recommended_fix: Expose eligible practitioner/resource availability or explicit “any practitioner” assignment with server-side collision rules.
source_risk_at_stake: Wrong practitioner assignment and unusable capacity model
source_business_impact: The UI/data model suggests teams while public booking is owner-centric.
source_existing_controls: Manual booking and practitioner membership exist.
source_why_controls_insufficient: Owner attribution is not a generalized scheduling/resource algorithm.
source_required_regression_tests: Specific/any practitioner, removed practitioner, service eligibility, parallel slots, no owner present.
source_reproduction: Add multiple practitioners and book publicly.

source_title: Pending invitation uniqueness is global by email

source_risk_at_stake: Invitation collision and cross-tenant operational leakage

source_affected_launch_scenarios: One user invited to multiple unrelated studios

source_title: CSV exports do not neutralize spreadsheet formulas

source_risk_at_stake: Spreadsheet formula execution or misleading content when opened
source_business_impact: Untrusted client-entered data can become active spreadsheet content.

source_affected_personas: Owners and support staff opening exports

source_title: Photo archive does not implement object purge or retention lifecycle

source_title: Typing a custom treatment area commits one partial area row per keystroke

source_evidence: supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql:82 sessions.practitioner_id references practitioners(id) on delete restrict; 0003_allergies_and_session_fields.sql:12 performed_by_practitioner_id references practitioners(id) on delete set null. 0094_tenant_consistency_constraints.sql adds composite same-studio FKs for client_id and appointment_id ONLY. 0160 names neither practitioner column.
